reasoning: By the pigeonhole principle, assigning 5 pigeons to 4 holes with at most one pigeon per hole is impossible because there are more pigeons than holes; at least one hole must contain multiple pigeons.
cot_trace: We are given a classic pigeonhole principle problem: 5 pigeons, 4 holes, each hole can contain at most one pigeon. So we need to assign each of the 5 pigeons to one of the 4 holes, with no hole having more than one pigeon. That means we need a one-to-one assignment from pigeons to holes, but there are more pigeons than holes. By the pigeonhole principle, this is impossible because there are 5 pigeons and only 4 holes, so at least one hole must contain at least two pigeons. Therefore, the problem is unsatisfiable. The answer should be UNSAT.
